meta.name: 036 - Severe Sepsis with Altered Mental Status

patient.name: Eleanor Voss
patient.chiefComplaint: Altered mental status and difficulty breathing

history.hpi: Daughter reports patient has seemed "off" and increasingly drowsy since yesterday, with fever, chills, and decreased urine output over the past two days. This morning she was difficult to arouse and her breathing appeared labored. No reported trauma, no seizure activity witnessed.
history.lastOralIntake: Sips of water this morning, no solid food since yesterday afternoon
history.events: Daughter found her difficult to arouse and called 911 after noting labored breathing and fever

scene.dispatch: 73-year-old female, altered mental status, difficulty breathing, residence
scene.location: Single-story home, patient found in bed in a dimly lit bedroom
scene.safety: No hazards to crew noted; cluttered bedside table with medications and soiled bedding
scene.bystanders: Daughter present, provides history, did not witness any seizure activity or trauma
visualCues: Labored, rapid breathing with accessory muscle use
Foley catheter bag with dark, cloudy urine visible at bedside

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew finds a 73-year-old female in bed, febrile, tachypneic with labored breathing, and minimally responsive to painful stimuli. Daughter reports two days of fever and decreased urine output preceding today's decline.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent but at risk; frequent secretions, weak cough
clinicalPresentation.breathing: Labored, rapid, shallow, accessory muscle use
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses weak and rapid, skin hot and flushed
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Withdraws to pain only, no purposeful movement
otherFindings: Foley catheter with dark, cloudy urine
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: Moans incomprehensibly to sternal rub, no verbal response

transitions.if: IV access and fluid bolus started
transitions.condition: Crew recognizes signs of distributive (septic) shock, establishes IV/IO access, checks blood glucose, and initiates rapid isotonic fluid boluses toward a MAP goal.

phases.name: Fluids and Access Started
phases.description: IV access is obtained, blood glucose checked, and rapid isotonic fluid boluses are underway targeting a MAP of 65 mmHg. Despite initial fluids, the patient's mental status and labored breathing do not improve, and airway reflexes remain unreliable.
phases.triggerCondition: After IV/IO access is established and the crew checks blood glucose and initiates predetermined 500 mL isotonic fluid boluses per the Shock guideline, working toward a MAP goal of 65 mmHg.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent but at risk; secretions persist, weak cough, no gag suppression noted
clinicalPresentation.breathing: Still labored and rapid despite fluids, accessory muscle use continues
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses improved but still rapid and thready
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Withdraws to pain only, no purposeful movement
otherFindings: IV access obtained, first 500 mL bolus infused
Blood glucose 132 mg/dL — no correction needed
Mental status unchanged despite fluid administration
Persistent risk for airway compromise given depressed mentation
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: Moans to sternal rub, no verbal response

expectedActions.shortAction: Establish IV access (IO if 2 failed attempts or >90 sec); check blood glucose and full vitals
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Check vital signs. Check blood sugar, and correct if less than 60 mg/dL. Establish IV access. If unable to obtain within two attempts or less than 90 seconds, place an IO needle
expectedActions.rationale: Confirms hypoglycemia is not a contributing cause of AMS and secures access for resuscitation before airway intervention.

expectedActions.shortAction: NS bolus 500 mL IV, repeat toward 2,040 mL (68 kg × 30 mL/kg) or MAP 65 mmHg
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Physiologic target: MAP goal 65 mmHg. Fluid goal of up to 30 mL/kg of isotonic fluid by administering rapid, predetermined boluses (e.g., 500 mL) unless the MAP goal is achieved, or pulmonary edema develops.
expectedActions.rationale: Early aggressive fluid resuscitation is the primary treatment for septic shock and should precede sedative/paralytic administration whenever possible to avoid peri-intubation hypotension.

expectedActions.shortAction: Provide advance notification to receiving hospital of suspected septic shock with impending airway management
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Provide advanced notification to the hospital
expectedActions.rationale: Allows the receiving facility to prepare resources for a critically ill septic patient requiring airway management.

transitions.condition: Despite fluid resuscitation, the patient remains obtunded (GCS 8) with an unreliable airway and labored breathing; the crew proceeds with rapid sequence intubation for airway protection after adequate fluid resuscitation.

The crew proceeds directly to RSI without completing adequate fluid resuscitation first; induction agents and positive pressure ventilation on top of unresuscitated shock precipitate abrupt hypotension.

phases.name: RSI Performed
phases.description: With airway reflexes unreliable and mentation unimproved despite fluids, the crew performs rapid sequence intubation for definitive airway protection, using ketamine for induction given its relative hemodynamic stability in shock.
phases.triggerCondition: Persistent altered mental status with loss of normal protective airway reflexes and labored breathing, despite ongoing fluid resuscitation, meets indication for RSI. The crew pre-oxygenates, premedicates, and administers induction and paralytic agents.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Secured with endotracheal tube, confirmed placement
clinicalPresentation.breathing: Ventilated via BVM/mechanical ventilator, symmetric chest rise
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present, improved strength after fluids
otherFindings: Endotracheal tube secured at appropriate depth

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize RSI indication: AMS with loss of protective airway reflexes, unresolved after fluids
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Other indications may include potential airway obstruction, severe inhalation burns, multiple traumatic injuries, altered mental status with loss of normal protective airway reflexes
expectedActions.rationale: Confirms the patient meets a specific protocol indication for definitive airway management rather than proceeding reflexively.

expectedActions.shortAction: Pre-oxygenate with high-flow O2 and PPV for at least 2 minutes prior to RSI
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Patient should be pre-oxygenated with high flow oxygen, and positive pressure ventilation for a minimum of two minutes prior to the procedure. In some circumstances, sedation may be required for adequate pre-oxygenation
expectedActions.rationale: Maximizes oxygen reserve to prevent peri-intubation hypoxia during the apneic period.

expectedActions.shortAction: Fentanyl 68 mcg IV (68 kg × 1 mcg/kg) 2-3 minutes prior to intubation attempt
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Consider pre-medication with Fentanyl, 1 mcg/kg, 2-3 minutes prior to intubation attempt.
expectedActions.rationale: Blunts the sympathetic/hemodynamic response to laryngoscopy.

expectedActions.shortAction: Ketamine 102 mg IV push (68 kg × 1.5 mg/kg, within 1-2 mg/kg range) for induction
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer induction sedative agent: Etomidate IV push, 0.2-0.3 mg/kg OR Ketamine IV push, 1-2 mg/kg OR Midazolam IV push, 0.05-0.10 mg/kg
expectedActions.rationale: Ketamine is favored here for its relative hemodynamic stability compared to other induction agents in a hypotensive, shock-prone patient.

expectedActions.shortAction: Rocuronium 68 mg IV push (68 kg × 1 mg/kg) as paralytic agent
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer paralytic agent: Succinylcholine IV push, 1-2 mg/kg OR Rocuronium IV push, 1 mg/kg OR Vecuronium IV push, 0.1 mg/kg
expectedActions.rationale: Provides paralysis to optimize intubating conditions after adequate sedation.

expectedActions.shortAction: Attempt intubation, limiting each attempt to 15 seconds or SpO2 <90%, whichever first
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Attempt intubation, limiting attempts to 15 seconds, or a desaturation below 90%, whichever occurs first
expectedActions.rationale: Prevents prolonged apnea and hypoxia during laryngoscopy attempts.

transitions.condition: Endotracheal tube placement is confirmed with waveform capnography and bilateral breath sounds; the tube is secured and mechanical ventilation is established, with stable hemodynamics maintained.

phases.name: Tube Confirmed, Stable Transport
phases.description: The airway is secured, ventilation and oxygenation are adequate, and the patient remains hemodynamically stable on ongoing fluids. Post-intubation sedation is maintained and the patient is transported with advance hospital notification.
phases.triggerCondition: Following confirmed endotracheal tube placement and stable post-intubation vitals, the crew provides ongoing sedation, continues fluid resuscitation as needed, and transports with continuous monitoring.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Secured, endotracheal tube in place and confirmed
clinicalPresentation.breathing: Mechanically ventilated, symmetric chest rise, EtCO2 within goal range
otherFindings: Tube secured and depth reassessed after each movement
Ongoing fluid resuscitation continued en route
Advance notification provided to receiving hospital

expectedActions.shortAction: Confirm ETT placement with waveform capnography and bilateral breath sounds; secure tube
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Confirm placement of advanced airway (endotracheal tube, SGA) with waveform capnography (most reliable), absent gastric sounds, and bilateral breath sounds
expectedActions.rationale: Waveform capnography is the most reliable confirmation method and reduces risk of unrecognized esophageal intubation.

expectedActions.shortAction: Post-intubation sedation: Fentanyl 68-136 mcg IV (1-2 mcg/kg) plus Midazolam 1.4 mg IV (0.02 mg/kg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Consider sedation with sedative and/or opioid medications if agitated: Fentanyl 1-2 mcg/kg And Midazolam 0.02 mg/kg
expectedActions.rationale: Maintains adequate sedation for the intubated, paralyzed patient during transport.

phases.name: RSI Without Fluid Resuscitation
phases.description: RSI is performed before adequate fluid resuscitation is completed. The combination of sedative-induced vasodilation, loss of sympathetic drive, and positive pressure ventilation on an unresuscitated septic patient precipitates abrupt, severe hypotension immediately after intubation.
phases.triggerCondition: Because fluid resuscitation was skipped or incomplete before RSI, induction and positive pressure ventilation unmask profound shock, causing the blood pressure to crash shortly after tube placement.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Mechanically ventilated, but perfusion critically impaired
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses absent, only faint central pulses palpable
otherFindings: Abrupt blood pressure drop noted immediately after intubation
Falling EtCO2 reflecting decreased pulmonary blood flow
No fluids infused prior to induction agents

expectedActions.shortAction: Rapid NS bolus 500 mL IV, reassess toward MAP 65 mmHg goal
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Fluid goal of up to 30 mL/kg of isotonic fluid by administering rapid, predetermined boluses (e.g., 500 mL) unless the MAP goal is achieved, or pulmonary edema develops.
expectedActions.rationale: Immediate fluid resuscitation is the first-line rescue for peri-intubation hypotension in an unresuscitated shock patient.

expectedActions.shortAction: Norepinephrine infusion 3.4 mcg/min (68 kg × 0.05 mcg/kg/min), titrate to MAP 65 mmHg
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Vasopressors (shock unresponsive to IV fluids) titrated to physiologic targets ... Norepinephrine 0.05–0.5 mcg/kg/minute ... Preference in both neurogenic and infectious (sepsis) causes of distributive shock
expectedActions.rationale: Norepinephrine is the preferred vasopressor for septic shock refractory to fluids alone.
